name: Volkov-Saito Precision VSP-11 'Stiletto'
description:
The VSP-11 Stiletto is a precision submachine gun — a contradiction in terms that Volkov-Saito makes work through obsessive engineering. The weapon fires 5.7mm caseless from a match-grade barrel with a precision bolt that locks into battery with the same consistency as their rifle platforms. The result is an SMG that delivers 2-MOA accuracy at 100 meters in semi-automatic mode — performance that rivals many assault rifles at that distance.

The Stiletto's BCI integration includes Volkov-Saito's signature weapon-learning system, building a ballistic profile specific to each individual weapon over time. The 20-round magazine feeds through a precision-machined feed ramp that eliminates the feeding inconsistencies common in SMG platforms. The trigger is a two-stage match unit adjustable from 1.5 to 3 kilograms.

At Φ7,500, the Stiletto costs more than many assault rifles. Its customers are operators who need SMG-class concealability with rifle-class accuracy — executive protection specialists who might need to make a 100-meter shot through a crowd without hitting bystanders, or covert operators who need precision from a compact platform. The VSP-11 does not spray. It places.
specifications:
caliber: 5.7mm caseless
effective_range: 200m
rate_of_fire: 750 rpm (cyclic), semi-auto preferred
magazine_capacity: 20 rounds
weight: 2.0 kg
tactical_use: The Stiletto enables precise engagements from a concealable platform. Its accuracy in semi-automatic mode allows operators to make shots that would require a rifle from other manufacturers' SMGs. In close protection scenarios where a missed shot hits a civilian, the VSP-11's precision is not a luxury — it is a requirement. The weapon-learning system improves accuracy over time, rewarding operators who maintain a consistent relationship with their specific weapon.
cultural_context: The Stiletto has a devoted following among precision-oriented operators who refuse to accept the accuracy limitations of conventional SMGs. Volkov-Saito's reputation for precision transfers directly to the VSP-11, and carrying one signals that the operator values placement over volume. In competitive shooting circles, Stiletto-class SMG matches have become a distinct discipline.
story_hooks: A VSP-11 was used to make an impossible shot through a crowded market — the 100-meter precision engagement hit only the intended target despite dozens of bystanders. Only a Stiletto with a trained operator could have made that shot.
Volkov-Saito's weapon-learning data from returned Stilettos has been compiled into a database that can identify individual operators by their firing patterns — an intelligence goldmine.

physical_description.visual_profile: A razor-thin, almost skeletal SMG with an aggressive forward rake. The Stiletto presents as a precision instrument disguised in a compact form — all hard angles and purposeful geometry. Its silhouette resembles a surgical blade more than a firearm, with a prominent top-mounted optical rail and minimal ergonomic flourish. The overall impression is cold, engineered, uncompromising.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 38 cm (stock collapsed), Barrel length: 15 cm, Width at receiver: 4.2 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly balanced despite its 2.0 kg mass — the weight concentrates forward into the match-grade barrel assembly, creating a natural pivot point that rewards practiced trigger control. Not light, but purposeful; every gram accounts for precision.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum receiver with carbon-composite furniture. Steel barrel and bolt assembly. Polymer grip frame with integrated capacitive sensor nodes for BCI linkage.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal grey with brushed titanium accents on the barrel shroud. The receiver shows a subtle cross-hatch machining pattern visible under harsh light — evidence of the precision manufacturing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey primary body with gunmetal steel barrel, platinum-silver BCI contact nodes along the grip, and subtle red accent lines marking the two-stage trigger housing.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with subtle ridging — not aggressive, designed for precise finger placement rather than vice-grip security. Capacitive nodes integrated into the grip material create a barely-perceptible tactile signature.
distinctive_features: Top-mounted full-length optical rail with integrated cable conduit for BCI neural link
Precision-machined feed ramp visible through a small dust cover window
Adjustable two-stage match trigger visible through the lower receiver opening
Micro-LED status indicators (green/amber/red) positioned on the right side of the receiver — barely noticeable unless active
Barrel shroud features three precision cooling vents arranged in a triangular pattern
Ambidextrous safety selector with tactical groove patterns
Weapon-learning dataport recessed flush in the grip tang — barely breaks the silhouette
Ultra-thin magazine with witness holes every two rounds for round count at a glance
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VOLKOV-SAITO PRECISION etched in Cyrillic-Latin hybrid script along the left side of the receiver. VSP-11 designation stamped on the barrel shroud. Serial number laser-engraved on the dust cover in microfont. Warranty seal at the magazine well.
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory-fresh examples show near-flawless finish with protective cosmoline residue. Field-maintained weapons develop a distinctive patina — wear marks on the charging handle, subtle polishing on the trigger guard from gloved use, occasional scorching on the barrel shroud from sustained semi-auto fire. The weapon-learning system means older examples develop individual character; no two veteran Stilettos look identical.
